rule.statement: Before taking any actions that update the booking database (booking, modifying flights, editing baggage, changing cabin class, or updating passenger information), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.

rules.why: The confirmation is in the conversation, and no argument of the write tools carries it.

rule.text: You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments.
You should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously.
If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time.
You should deny user requests that are against this policy.

rule.statement: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions.

rules.why: Whether a request is in the scope of the agent's actions is a reading of the case; the summary argument does not decide it.

rule.statement: If the status is delayed or on time, the flight has not taken off, cannot be booked. If the status is flying, the flight has taken off but not landed, cannot be booked.

rules.why: The status belongs to one flight on one date inside the array flights and is read from a search result; no typed rule reads an array of flight and date pairs.

rule.statement: Each reservation can have at most five passengers.

rules.why: The limit is on the number of items of the array passengers; threshold compares a number argument and no typed rule counts items.

rule.statement: Each reservation can use at most one travel certificate, at most one credit card, and at most three gift cards.

rules.why: The limits count the items of the array payment_methods per kind of payment method; no typed rule counts items of an array.

rule.statement: All payment methods must already be in user profile for safety reasons.

rules.why: The ids are inside the array payment_methods and membership takes one id argument; the profile is a get_user_details result.

rule.statement: Checked bag allowance: If the booking user is a regular member: 0 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger, 1 free checked bag for each economy passenger, 2 free checked bags for each business passenger. If the booking user is a silver member: 1 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger, 2 free checked bag for each economy passenger, 3 free checked bags for each business passenger. If the booking user is a gold member: 2 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger, 3 free checked bag for each economy passenger, 4 free checked bags for each business passenger. Each extra baggage is 50 dollars.

rules.why: The free bags depend on the membership level in the profile and on the number of passengers; derived_value reads only arguments of the call, and neither is a number argument of book_reservation.

rule.quote: Basic economy flights cannot be modified.

rules.quote: Basic economy flights cannot be modified.

rule.statement: Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type.

rules.why: The call names flight numbers only; origin, destination and trip type of the stored reservation and of the new flights are in tool results.

rule.statement: Cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.

rules.why: Flown or not is a fact of each flight on its date, read with get_flight_status; no typed rule reads every flight of a reservation.

rule.statement: In other cases, all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights.

rules.why: The same tool changes flights and cabin; a change of flights is seen only by comparing the array flights with the stored reservation.

rule.statement: The user can add but not remove checked bags.

rules.why: The new total must be compared with the stored total; threshold compares an argument with a fixed value only.

rule.statement: The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers.

rules.why: The number of items of the array passengers must be compared with the stored reservation; no typed rule counts items or compares with a record.

rule.statement: If the flights are changed, the user needs to provide a single gift card or credit card for payment or refund method.

rules.why: The kind of payment holds only if the flights are changed; a format rule has no such condition, and the same tool also changes only the cabin.

rule.statement: If the flights are changed, the user needs to provide a single gift card or credit card for payment or refund method. The payment method must already be in user profile for safety reasons.

rules.why: The call has payment_id and reservation_id but no user id for membership; the profile is a get_user_details result.

rule.statement: If any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.

rules.why: Flown or not is a fact of each flight on its date, read with get_flight_status; no typed rule reads every flight of a reservation.

rule.statement: Otherwise, flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true: The booking was made within the last 24 hrs. The flight is cancelled by airline. It is a business flight. The user has travel insurance and the reason for cancellation is covered by insurance.

rules.why: The test is an any-of over the created time, the flight status, the cabin, the insurance and the stated reason; record_condition tests one field and cancel_reservation has only an id argument.

rule.statement: Do not proactively offer a compensation unless the user explicitly asks for one.

rules.why: Whether the user asked is in the conversation; no argument of send_certificate carries it.

rule.statement: Do not compensate if the user is regular member and has no travel insurance and flies (basic) economy. Only compensate if the user is a silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business.

rules.why: The test joins the membership level in the profile with the insurance and the cabin of the reservation; record_condition tests one field of one record.

rule.statement: Always confirms the facts before offering compensation.

rules.why: Confirming the facts is a sequence of earlier reads and replies; no argument of send_certificate carries it.

rule.statement: If the user complains about cancelled flights in a reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture after confirming the facts, with the amount being $100 times the number of passengers.

rules.why: The amount depends on the number of passengers of the reservation, which send_certificate does not carry; derived_value reads only arguments.

rule.statement: If the user complains about delayed flights in a reservation and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture after confirming the facts and changing or cancelling the reservation, with the amount being $50 times the number of passengers.

rules.why: The amount depends on the number of passengers, and the order after the change or cancellation is a sequence of calls; no typed rule reads both.

rule.statement: Do not offer compensation for any other reason than the ones listed above: complaints about cancelled flights in a reservation, and complaints about delayed flights in a reservation from a user who wants to change or cancel the reservation.

rules.why: The reason for a certificate is in the conversation; no argument of send_certificate carries it.

global_rules.rule: Before taking any actions that update the booking database (booking, modifying flights, editing baggage, changing cabin class, or updating passenger information), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.
You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments.
You should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously.
If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time.
You should deny user requests that are against this policy.

escalation.name: Transfer to a human agent
steps: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions.
To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user.

There are two types of trip: one way and round trip.

policy_questions.question: The list of actions that update the booking database does not name a cancellation or a certificate. Must the agent also list the details and obtain a yes before cancel_reservation and send_certificate?

When a request is against this policy, the agent should deny it, and when it cannot be handled within the scope of its actions, the agent should transfer. Which of the two applies to a request that the policy forbids and no tool can do, such as adding insurance after booking?
Does 'cannot be booked' also hold for a new flight chosen in update_reservation_flights, and for a kept segment that is delayed, on time or flying?
Can a reservation that is not basic economy change its flights and its cabin in the same change, or must the flights stay the same whenever the cabin changes?

The payment statements start with 'If the flights are changed'. Do the single gift card or credit card and the user profile also hold for a change of cabin only, and for added bags in update_reservation_baggages, whose payment_id description also gives a certificate as an example?
The free bag table and the 50 dollars are in the section Book flight. Do they also set nonfree_baggages and the price when bags are added later with update_reservation_baggages?
Does 'already been flown' include a flight with the status flying, which has taken off but not landed? The text defines no status for a flight that has landed.
'The flight is cancelled by airline': is the reason that the user states enough, or must a flight record show it? The listed flight statuses do not include a cancelled status.
'The agent can offer a certificate': when the user asks, is eligible and the facts are confirmed, must the agent send the certificate, or may the agent still decide not to?

The remaining amount of a travel certificate is not refundable, and the refund goes to original payment methods. When a reservation paid with a travel certificate is cancelled, does the certificate part of the payment come back?
Must the amounts in payment_methods add up to the flight prices plus the extra bags and the insurance? The text gives the prices of bags and insurance but no rule for the total.
